static_traits.name: Li Manning
static_traits.family_status: From a large family with 8 brothers; parents over 80; close to family, but relationship tension with one brother since the roof-repair incident
static_traits.social_status: The family as a whole is fairly supportive, but the client finds it hard to discuss inadequacy and inferiority with family
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior psychotherapy history
static_traits.language_features: Positive attitude, clear expression, able to reflect and cooperate, able to describe events and emotional experiences concretely

basic_info.main_problem: After trying to help his brother repair the house but making things worse, labeling himself a 'useless handyman', with the resulting sense of inadequacy extending to other areas of life, affecting confidence and daily tasks.
basic_info.core_demands: 'I really want to change the way I think about myself and feel better about my abilities.' (I want to change how I see myself and be able to view my own abilities with more confidence)
growth_experiences: Family of origin: has 8 brothers, parents in their 80s, family fairly supportive, but the client says it is hard to discuss inadequacy and inferiority with family (long-term family atmosphere and support characteristics).

Positive experience: last month before this incident, the client helped a younger brother complete a school project, earning the other's recognition and good grades; this successful helping experience boosted the client's self-efficacy.

special_situations.event: While helping the older brother repair a roof leak, an operational mistake caused roof damage, further triggering the brother's disappointment and blame
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make mistakes while helping or have not done it right, it proves I am useless, better not to help
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Works hard beforehand to perform well and leave a good impression; afterwards proactively offers to make amends and help again to repair the impression
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am too useless, I should not have helped, I disappointed him

special_situations.event: Whenever recalling the failure of roof repair or facing tasks requiring hands-on ability
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I try again, I will definitely fail again, and disappoint others again
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids or procrastinates on tasks; before starting, worries excessively and thinks repeatedly to reduce risk
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely mess up again, better not to do it

special_situations.event: When helping cook at home, stays tense and distracted from worrying about mistakes, and ends up burning the food
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot achieve perfection, it equals failure and proves I'm no good
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessively monitoring every step, attending to errors in order to avoid making mistakes, resulting in scattered attention and operational errors
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely break it this time; I always mess up

special_situations.event: While carrying out other daily tasks and chores, generalizes from one failed roof repair to ability judgments in other domains
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One failure means I do not do well in other areas either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Lowers willingness to try, reduces taking on tasks to avoid disproving one's own ability again

core_conflict.wish: Longs to gain recognition and acceptance from significant others through competence and helping (especially the elder brother)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and disappointing others, thus being negated as 'useless'
defense_goal: Avoids failing again and disappointing others through self-belittlement and reduced attempts
Maintains a sense of safety and controllability in relationships through excessive self-blame and internalized criticism

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about the failed roof repair or invited in counseling to review failure details and self-feelings
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Internalizing others' disappointment and criticism as negation of overall self-worth, believing 'I am just useless'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a gentle, empathic tone, first validating shame and self-blame; avoiding judgment and hasty correction, inviting distinguishing 'ability' from 'one outcome' with concrete facts and situations, encouraging identifying the inner critic's voice.

manifestations: Although overall family support, the client finds it hard to discuss inadequacy and inferiority with family
Strongly longing for the brother's recognition, experiencing isolation and shaken self-worth when not yet recognized
outcomes: Impaired sense of self-worth, anxiety and increased self-doubt
Withdrawal and avoidance tendencies arising in tasks requiring hands-on ability

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Worries excessively about disappointing others, thereby reducing attempts or self-limiting before the task begins
In narration, focuses on mistakes and failures, ignoring existing evidence of success and ability

exception_events.target_problem: In situations requiring helping others or hands-on tasks, the client usually anticipates failure, developing strong anxiety and thus performing poorly or avoiding.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Last month, the client successfully helped his younger brother complete a school project; the brother was satisfied and got good grades, and the engagement and sense of achievement during the process were different from the usual 'I will mess up' experience.
exception_events.reason: Different task situation: the academic project better matched current ability; different support: receiving timely positive feedback and recognition; different state: relatively lower anxiety, more focused attention.

positive_force: The family overall is quite supportive, has dependable social support resources
Has had successful experiences helping others (helped younger brother complete a project), has real evidence of ability
Willing to seek help, positive attitude, willing to do cognitive testing and restructuring
Able to identify and describe one's own negative automatic thoughts and emotional experiences, with some self-reflection ability
negative_force: Self-labeling and overgeneralization (one failure extended to overall ability)
Personalization and high sensitivity to others' disappointment, excessively bears responsibility
Catastrophizing and predicting failure, marked pre-task anxiety, affecting attention and performance
Excessive self-monitoring and self-limitation, leading to avoiding attempts and declining confidence

target_behavior.behavior: Strong anxiety and negative self-talk before tasks requiring hands-on work or helping others (such as 'I am very useless' / 'I will mess up')
antecedent: Asked by family for help or starts tasks like housework/cooking
Recalls the failed roof repair and the older brother's disappointment and blame
When minor errors or uncertain moments occur during the task
target_behavior.core_reason: After one significant failure, developing overgeneralization and personalization biases, highly sensitive to disappointing others, forming catastrophic anticipation of failing again
target_behavior.function: Short-term avoidance of potential failure and negative external evaluation, maintaining brief psychological safety
target_behavior.consequence: Declining performance (such as distracted attention, burning food), damaged self-confidence, tense interpersonal relationships (with the brother)

target_behavior.behavior: Self-deprecating negative self-talk ('I cannot do anything well' / 'I am a useless person')
antecedent: Thinking of the roof-repair incident or hearing others' dissatisfaction and blame
When starting new tasks or facing unfamiliar housework
target_behavior.core_reason: Using one failure as evidence for global negation, internalizing others' disappointment as judgment of overall self-worth
target_behavior.function: Avoiding stronger external negation and disappointment by lowering expectations and self-positioning
target_behavior.consequence: Lowered self-esteem, avoiding challenges, negative emotions persisting and expanding
